headline: Approved $500 from Veterans Commission funds toward a shortfall for the Global War on Terror remembrance ceremony.
summary: Plans for the November 10 Veterans Day event include a plaque for fallen soldier John F. Landry Jr. Other events discussed were a Truck or Treat display on October 27 and a City of Lights Parade float on November 28. The commission also approved a letter to UMass President Martin Meehan and the September minutes.
decisions: Approved a $500 donation from Veterans Commission funds toward the cost of the Global War on Terror event, by unanimous vote.
Moved the next meeting from 11/11/26 to 11/18/26 because of the Veterans Day holiday.
Approved a letter to UMass President Martin Meehan about the UMass Lowell Hockey Night vendor table.
Approved Wreaths Across America Mobile Education Van display at the 2027 Veterans Day Event.
Approved the minutes of the September Veterans Commission meeting.

plain_text:
MINUTES
LOWELL VETERANS COMMISSION
DATE: Wednesday, 14th of October 2026 at 5:05 PM
Location: Council Chambers Lowell City Hall
Meeting:
a. Call to Order: 5:05 PM
b. Pledge of Allegiance
c. Roll Call Attendance
PARADISE, PAUL
GAFFNEY, JAMES III
COTE, RICHARD A.
HARMON, JAMES (NOT IN ATTENDANCE)
PEEPLES, MICHAEL
CEROVAC, ROBERT
GAUTHIER, PHILIAS
PIMENTEL, NAYELI  (NOT IN ATTENDANCE)
PEEPLES, JEAN, SUB COMMITTEE MEMBER
ERIC LAMARCHE, DIRECTOR OF VETERANS SERVICES
STEVEN PANAGIOTAKOS, FORMER STATE SENATOR FROM LOWELL
Discussion:
1. Guest Speaker:
Steven Panagiotakos, former State Senator from Lowell spoke to the members of the Veterans Commission 
about the upcoming Veterans Day event on November 10, 2026, at the Lowell Memorial Auditorium being 
held at 10:00 AM.  During the ceremony fallen soldier John F. Landry Jr. of Lowell will be honored with a 
plaque that will be unveiled in the Hall of Flags at the Lowell Memorial Auditorium.  Steven reported there 
are 1,278 fallen soldiers from Lowell.  They are all honored with a plaque at the auditorium, but there is one
plaque missing.  Thanks to the efforts of Steve, there will be a plaque placed in the Hall of Flags due to the 
donations made possible by Steve.  Those same donors will also provide refreshments during the event.
2. Chairman Paul Paradise reported that he and the Veterans Commission members attended the Global War on
Terror 25th Year Remembrance Ceremony featuring the UAV Fallen Heros Memorial that was hosted by the 
Lowell Vet Center.  Chairman Paradise was honored to be the police escort for the arrival and departure of 
the memorial.  UAV Fallen Heros Memorial was impressive.  The memorial included the Dog Tags with the 
Names of all of the fallen soldiers from the Global War on Terror designed in the shape of the American 
Flag.  Chairman Paradise echoed the heartfelt thanks from Dr. Elizabeth Parrot, Director of the Lowell Vet 
Center and Tiffany Lever, Veterans Outreach Program Specialist for the support of the Veterans 
Commission during the event.  A shortfall of funding for the event was discussed, and a vote was taken to 
donate $500 from the Veterans Commission funds to help with the cost of the event, which was met with a 
unanimous vote of approval (given that the Law Department of the City of Lowell approves).
3. The meeting place of future Veterans Commission meetings was discussed as the Lowell Telemedia Center 
is still under construction following a water leak.  Sub Committee Member Jean Peeples will contact Adam 
at the LTC about resuming meetings.  The next meeting of the Veterans Commission has been changed from
11/11/26 to 11/18/26 due to the Veterans Day Holiday.  If the LTC is not yet available, Veterans Commission
Member Jay Gaffney will try to book the Mayor’s Reception Room if available for our next meeting 
11/18/26, with subsequent meetings being held on the 2nd Wednesday of the month possibly at the LTC.
4. The Veterans Commission will be participating in the Truck or Treat event on 10/27/26 at 4:00 PM at the 
American Legion Post # 247, Tyngsboro MA, which is being hosted by the Lowell Vet Center.  The theme 
of the display will be a depiction from the movie “Animal House” and candy will be given out to all guests.
Veterans Commission members will be dressed up as characters from the movie.  The Veterans Commission
pop up banner will be on display.
5. Chairman Paradise report about a veteran’s event at St. Michael’s Church, Bridge Street Lowell, MA on 
11/9/26 at 8:00 AM featuring a luncheon to honor veterans, questions and answers from veterans regarding 
their service to our country, and children singing to honor veterans.  All are welcome.
6. The Veterans Commission will be hosting a float in the City of Lights Parade Saturday, 11/28/26 starting at 
Jackson Street.  The Committee for the City of Lights Parade may provide a banner…Sponsored by the 
Lowell Veterans Commission.  The Veterans Commission members will be decorating a Holiday Tree in red,
white and blue lights.  A flatbed trailer/truck will be decorated with flags, patriotic bunting, and Military 
logos.  Veteran Commission members are welcome to ride on the float, and a generator will be provided to 
equip the float with electricity for heaters and lighting of the tree.  Veteran Commission member Phil 
Gauthier offered to provide candy to be given to the spectators.  Timing and the place for decorating the 
float prior to the parade is needed.  Sophia Bourcher is the point person fot this event.
7. Eric Lamarche and Paul Paradise updated the Veterans Commission about the upcoming Veterans Day 
Event hosted by the Veterans Commission on 11/10/26 at the Lowell Memorial Auditorium at 10:00 AM.  
Details of the planning of the event include:
 Refreshments will be provided due to the fundraising efforts of Senator Steven 
Panagiotakos and other supporters.
 Military music will be played prior to start of event and will be displayed on the video 
screen featuring a tribute to Lowell Veterans provided by the CASE Office of the City of 
Lowell.
 Guest speakers:
Mayor Erik Gitschier
City Manager Thomas A. Golden, Jr.
Eric Lemarch, Director of Veterans Services
Paul Paradise, Chairman of the Veterans Commission Lowell MA
Senator Steven Panagiotakos
 Pledge of Allegiance will be recited.
 Imogene Stulken, Minister, Campus Ministries at UMass Lowell to perform the 
Benediction.
 Fallen Soldier John F. Landry, Jr., will be honored with a plaque which will be unveiled 
at the Lowell Memorial Auditorium Hall of Flags. A wreath honoring Landry will be on 
display and a bouquet of flowers will be present to his family.
 Invited participants include:
Ted Serozynsky, Director Military and Veteran Services UMass Lowell
Lt. Col. Jovon, Commander AFROTC Detachment 345 UMass Lowell
Honor Guard Lowell Police Department
Lowell High School ROTC
Speaker from Lowell Catholic High School to speak about the plaque dedication to 
Veteran Landry
Hidden Battles
National Guard
The Bridge Club
 The Veterans Commission will host a vendor table with veteran services information, 
poppy give way, patriotic gum give away, and patriotic decorations (including the 
Veterans Commission pop up banner).
8. The Veterans Recognition Program was reviewed.  Commission member James Gaffney has provided the 
following criteria for the program:  A Distinguished Lowell Veteran is a military veteran who has served 
honorably in the Armed forces of the United States of America and has made a significant contribution to 
the city or its residents. Lowell residence is not a requirement, but the contribution must be to this city.
9. Paul Paradise provided details of a Lowell High School ROTC Student and Lowell Police Cadet’s life 
saving heroics in saving an autistic child from drowning.  The City of Lowell has honored the student, yet 
the Veterans Commission would like to invite her to a meeting and show appreciation for her life saving 
heroics, commitment to community service and our nation.  Details will be discussed at a future meeting.
10. The Veterans Commission would like to host a Vendor table at the UMass of Lowell Hockey Night during 
their Veterans Appreciation Night with a giant thank you card for guests to sign for the Veterans at the 
Veterans Administration Hospital in Bedford MA.  Vice Chairman Robert Cerovac approved a letter to 
President Martin Meehan of the University of Massachusetts to help coordinate this event, as well as asking 
for support of the students to join in the events of the Veterans Commission and help support the 
community.  Vice Chairman Cerovac also suggested a copy of the letter be sent to the Chancellor of UMass 
Lowell.  The letter was approved by Vice Chairman Cerovac and by Chairman Paul Paradise.  Veterans 
Commission Secretary Michael Peeples will send the letters right away.
11. The Veterans Commission would like to host a Vendor table at the Golden Gloves Veterans Appreciation 
Night as well.
12. Veterans Commission member Jay Gaffney reports he invited a guest speaker to our next meeting, Emily 
Forbes of the Veterans Administration.
13. Eric Lemarche reviewed that the Banner Program was going well and also reminded all Veterans that he can
provide assistance to Veterans in need such as financial assistant, help with rent, claims for Veterans 
Administration compensation, and much more.
14. Paul Paradise reviewed that he could provide Veterans with resources as well such placement for homeless 
Veterans and much more.
15. Paul Paradise reported that James Harmon and Nayeli Pimental resigned from the Veterans Commission.
16. New Business:
a. Meet and Greet invites to speak at the Veterans Commission meetings.  After the elections potential 
invitees include our State Representatives.
b. Secure the Lowell Memorial Auditorium for next year’s Veterans Day Event 11/10/27.
c. Wreaths Across America Mobile Education Van has been approved to be on display during the 2027 
Veterans Day Event.  A confirmation was received and they will update the Veterans Commission.
d. The ordering of a Banner for future events: “Sponsored by the Veterans Commission of Lowell” will 
be put in place soon.
e. Approval of meeting Minutes of Veterans Commission meeting of September was granted.
17. Conclusion:
Move to adjourn. Adjourned Time: 5:45 PM
a. Move –Chairman Paul Paradise
b. 2nd –Secretary, Michael Peepl
c. Unanimous approval
________________________________________________________________________________________
Regularly scheduled meetings of the Lowell Veterans Commission are held on the 2nd Wednesday of the 
month Lowell TeleMedia Center, 246 Market St, Lowell, MA 01852 starting at 5:00 PM. The following is 
a list of scheduled meetings: September 9, 2026, October 14, 2026, November 11, 2026 (rescheduled to 
November 18, 2026), December 9, 2026, January 13, 2027, February 10, 2027, March 10, 2027, April 14, 
2027, May 12, 2027, and. June 9, 2027.
